question: Do the SEARCA 2002 Calancan Bay monograph and related SEAFDEC account provide a usable species-level or current fish baseline?

sources.title: Ripples of Hope over Troubled Waters: The Calancan Bay Experience

access.reportedFishEvidence: The accessible text of the monograph reports a visual fish census with 82 fish species in 22 families and 1,846 individuals across sample stations in Calancan Bay. It does not establish the fish survey date, list-level identity, station-by-taxon linkage, coordinate precision, or a complete effort description in the portions verified.
relatedWorksCited: SEAMEO SEARCA and DENR (1998), Integrated Area Management Plan for Calancan Bay
SEARCA and DENR (1998), Environmental Profile of Calancan Bay

reuse.metadata: Cite the publisher record and listed authors.
reuse.raw: No copy, species table, figure, or image was downloaded into the repository.
reuse.content: The official page offers a free-download workflow, but no item-specific open license was found. Free access does not establish reuse rights. The official form requests reason and personal details; it was not completed. No table-derived app reuse is approved.

caveats: The 82-species aggregate is reported in an accessible third-party copy and has not been checked against a publisher-supplied full text.
Do not treat 82 as a normalized checklist, present-day presence, catch recommendation, or independently validated count.
The monograph cites two separate 1998 SEARCA/DENR reports; their tables, methods, scope and rights were not retrieved.
The 2002 publication year is not confirmed as the fish sampling year.
No freshwater river, lake, reservoir or wetland evidence is established by this marine bay assessment.

sources.title: SEAFDEC Asian Aquaculture, Volume 23(5-6), September-December 2001: seagrass feature referencing Calancan Bay
authors: Milagros T. Castaños (editor; individual feature author not independently identified)
sources.publication: SEAFDEC Aquaculture Department magazine, 2001, pp. 31-33 of the scanned issue

access.reportedEvidence: The feature describes artificial seagrass units at Calancan Bay and reports that the fish species count associated with the units was 46% of that recorded in nearby natural seagrass and 86% of transplanted seagrass areas. The caption refers to a Marinduque mine-tailings bay site in 1998.

reuse.metadata: Cite the SEAFDEC repository record and issue details.
reuse.raw: The official repository PDF was viewed but not copied into the repository.
reuse.content: The repository labels the PDF Open Access, but no item-specific reuse license was located. Do not infer a right to republish text, images, or derived tables from access status alone.

caveats: This is a historical habitat-restoration summary, not a fish checklist or standardized bay-wide census.
Relative percentages have no absolute species counts or taxon list in the reviewed passage.
The reported comparison cannot be used to infer current abundance, recruitment, fishery yield, or site safety.

integrityFindings.historicalCountComparison: The 2002 SEARCA text reports 82 species; the separate 1990 NFRDI paper reports 85 visually recorded species, 108 in its abstract/index, and 72 manually counted Table 4 labels including unresolved entries. Their totals and sampling frames are not reconciled and must remain separate.
integrityFindings.1998ReportAccessLead: The 2002 monograph cites a 1998 Calancan Bay Environmental Profile and a 1998 Integrated Area Management Plan. Recover the original reports before attempting to validate or reuse the 82-species aggregate.
integrityFindings.currentStatus: Neither historical source establishes current fish presence, safe consumption, water quality, catchability, fishing rules, or public access.

limits: The SEARCA publisher page describes the monograph as free to download, but the download form was not completed and the official full text was not obtained.
The 82-species figure was visible only in a third-party text copy; the underlying fish table, exact survey period, methods and station map remain unverified.
The SEAFDEC magazine passage reports only relative species richness in artificial seagrass, with no species names, totals, dates or sampling details.
The sources cover marine bay and seagrass settings and do not fill the Marinduque inland-water evidence gap.
No license was established for transforming either source's table or text into a public app dataset.

followUp.nextAction: The bounded search for both cited 1998 reports did not locate an original copy; see mimaropa-calancan-bay-1998-report-retrieval-review-20261105.json. Keep the titles as archival leads, but do not block other independently sourced MIMAROPA work while access is unresolved. Keep marine and inland evidence separate and do not publish historical totals as current presence.
